terra.problem: Moses predicts what the officials will say; the passage does not report them saying it later.
The oven comparison does not match the proposed condition. Leaving a bakery while its ovens stay behind would ordinarily be possible.
“Close to the neighborhood” is unclear: the cattle and sheep answer has no evident connection to that phrase.
The joke gives Papa Dorin neighbors, although he lives alone on his cookie planet.
Not snarling does not mean the dogs hold their barks.
The message says the dogs will not snarl; it does not say they will be calm.
Moses, not the LORD, says he will depart after the officials speak.
The passage does not say Pharaoh's officials previously told the Israelites to stay and keep working.
“No strings attached” asserts that the officials will impose no conditions. Moses does not say that.
Aaron is called Moses' brother without a reference for that fact, which is not stated in this passage.
The instructions do not say that nobody gets left out.
The blood goes on the doorframes of the houses where they eat the lambs, not necessarily each person's own home.
The passage specifies the doorframes of the houses where they eat the lambs, not necessarily their own front doors.
“No secrets in this meal” goes beyond the text. The instruction specifies haste, not whether anything is secret.
The passage does not say that every time they eat unleavened bread, they remember the departure from Egypt.
The text reports that the people bowed down and worshiped; it does not say they did not push back.
Aaron is called Moses' brother without a reference for that fact, which is outside this passage. The final explanation also does not say the story is not over.
